text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, five activities — A19, A22, A23, A24 and A25 — each ran in a minority of traces (A19 and A22 in 45 of 200, A24 in 42, A25 in 40, A23 in 31) and behaved as mutually exclusive alternatives: pairs of them shared a trace in at most about 0.5 in 100 cases. In the later window each of them is nearly unobserved (0–2 of 200 traces). [OCC001, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL003, REL005, REL031, REL039, REL044]
- Five other activities — A20, A21, A30, A31 and A32 — were not observed in any of the 200 earlier traces, but each appears in about 97–98 in 100 later traces, essentially once per trace. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]
- In the later window the new five run together in the same traces: every pair co-occurs in about 97–98 in 100 traces, and both orders occur in similar proportions (for example A20 precedes A21 in about 46 in 100 traces and A21 precedes A20 in about 52 in 100), so the group has no fixed internal order. [REL012, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL026, REL028, REL053, REL054, REL057]
- The group sits between the same anchors that framed the old activities. In the earlier window A48 preceded A19, A22 and A24 in about 21–22 in 100 traces, and those activities preceded A33 in about 21–22 in 100; in the later window A48 precedes each of A20, A21, A30, A31 and A32 in about 95–97 in 100 traces, and each of them precedes A33 in about 95–97 in 100. [REL010, REL011, REL020, REL021, REL029, REL030, REL037, REL038, REL048, REL049, REL055, REL056, REL058, REL059, REL060, REL061]
- A48's outgoing transitions shifted accordingly: about 93 in 100 of its observed outgoing edges went to A19, A22, A23, A24 or A25 in the earlier window, while about 91 in 100 go to A20, A21, A30, A31 or A32 in the later window; the dense mutual transitions among the new activities and A33 (successor shares of roughly 15–26 in 100 each) are visible only in the later window. [DIR009, DIR002, DIR003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- Consistent with a larger block inserted between the anchors, A33's mean relative position moved later (about 0.43 to 0.48) and A48's moved earlier (about 0.36 to 0.31), with both activities still occurring in every trace. [POS011, POS012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the segment between A48 and A33 is executed with a different set of activities: the mutually exclusive optional activities A19, A22, A23, A24 and A25, which each ran in roughly 15–23 in 100 earlier traces between A48 and A33, are replaced by a group of five activities — A20, A21, A30, A31 and A32 — that now run together in nearly every trace, in no fixed internal order, between A48 and A33. The change is shown directly by relational and directional evidence (A48 before the group and the group before A33 in each window), it is consistent across the occurrence, direction, position and relation indicators (which partly reflect the same traces), participation moved from 0 to about 97–98 in 100 traces, and the screening yielded 92 qualifying items where roughly 1 would be expected without a change — far beyond what sampling differences between two 200-trace windows produce. [OCC002, OCC006, DIR009, POS011, POS012, REL012, REL020, REL021]

Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window shows only that A20, A21 and A30–A32 were not observed there, not that they were absent from the process, so a shift in the mix of pre-existing variants (a rare new-block path missed by the earlier sample) cannot be fully ruled out; the residual 1–2 later traces containing the old activities also show they were not strictly removed. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC007]

Other differences: in the two residual later traces containing A19, its outgoing transitions split between A33 and A07, and A22's residual traces lead to A33 and A05; with only two traces each, these differences are too weak to interpret. [DIR001, DIR004]
